why: The textbook k-way merge: keep the current head of every list in a min-heap; repeatedly pop the smallest node, append it to the output and push its successor. The week's linked-list part is relinking existing nodes instead of copying values.
hints: At any moment the next output node is the smallest among the k current heads.
A min-heap of (value, list index, node) gives that smallest head in O(log k); after popping, push that node's next.
Append popped nodes to a tail pointer. O(N log k) time for N total nodes, O(k) heap. (Pairwise divide-and-conquer merging has the same complexity.)
pitfalls: Empty lists (None heads) must be skipped when building the heap, and an empty outer array returns None.
Put the list index in the heap tuple: ListNode objects cannot be compared when values tie.
Keep duplicates: every original node appears once in the result.
